case.case_title: Wijeratne v. Vijitha Perera, Sub-Inspector of Police, Polonnaruwa and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 379/93, decided on 10 January 1994

clause.text: Freedom of speech and expression including publication.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the seizure of leaflets and threats to the petitioner infringed his fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression under Article 14(1)(a).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that the seizure of his posters and threats to remand him if he proceeded with the picketing campaign violated his freedom of speech and expression.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied arrest and detention and claimed the petitioner was warned not to create disturbances but could carry on a peaceful picketing campaign.
key_facts: Petitioner was secretary of a trade union branch and planned a peaceful picketing campaign with posters.
Police searched petitioner's house without a warrant or consent and seized posters.
Posters contained workers' demands and nothing subversive or criminal.
Petitioner was threatened with remand if posters were displayed and was detained overnight.
The seizure and threats deterred the planned peaceful protest.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 14(1)(a) protects the right to freedom of speech and expression, including peaceful protest and publication of materials. The seizure of posters and threats to the petitioner constituted an unlawful restriction on this right.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the seizure of posters unlawful as they contained only legitimate demands and no objectionable content. The threats and detention were intended to suppress lawful dissent and thus violated the petitioner’s freedom of speech and expression.
principles_established: Freedom of speech includes the right to communicate disagreement openly by peaceful and lawful means.
Law enforcement must not suppress lawful dissent or peaceful protest.
Seizure of materials used for peaceful protest without lawful authority is unlawful.
precedents_cited: West Virginia State Board of Education v. Barnette (1943) 319 US 624

outcome.holding: The court held that the seizure of posters and threats to the petitioner infringed his fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression under Article 14(1)(a).
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Compensation of Rs. 70,000 awarded to the petitioner; directions issued to police to respect fundamental rights.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 14(1)(a) was central to the court's reasoning as the case concerned the unlawful seizure of protest materials and suppression of peaceful expression, directly implicating freedom of speech and expression.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found that the posters contained nothing subversive or objectionable and that their seizure and the threats to remand the petitioner were unlawful and infringed his rights under Article 14(1)(a).
